title: land and the sync gate record their steps and times
goal: backlog.py land appends one ops row per step it runs (item id, step, exit, milliseconds) and one land.end row with the total and the lane; kbgit.py sync appends one sync.gate row per run holding each check's name, whether it ran, why it was skipped, its exit and milliseconds, the selected test scope and the push outcome.
notes: Failures it answers: gates and lands that waited about 40 minutes with no record of which step or whose run (ST-zkotxvdl), and a gate that dropped its git scenarios with nothing printed about the selected scope (BG-7ods5qqd). Merged finding (SP-djri7fqp retro): a sprint cost report printed zeros for eleven items worked in hand-made worktrees without capture hooks, so the review could show nothing. land warns when an item lands with no work rows in the ops rows, so a missing hook is caught at the landing and not at the review.
